samples.summary: Theme value read from localStorage is hardened against throws but still not validated before being applied to the DOM
samples.evidence: The diff wraps the read in `readStoredTheme()` (returns `string | null`) but the caller still blind-casts it: `return (readStoredTheme(storageKey) as Theme) || defaultTheme;` (theme-provider.tsx:65). That value flows unvalidated into `root.classList.add(theme)` (theme-provider.tsx:87). Compare the sibling module added in the same change, which does validate (`isFormat()` in src/lib/date-format-preference.ts:26-28,51). Vector: any same-origin script able to write `localStorage["vite-ui-theme"]` (a third-party dependency, a browser extension content script, or a transient XSS wanting persistence) chooses an arbitrary class name applied to `<html>` on every subsequent load — attacker-chosen Tailwind/utility classes can hide, move, or overlay trusted UI (clickjacking-style bait for the document-delete confirmations), and a value containing a space or empty string raises `InvalidCharacterError` out of the effect, breaking the app persistently. Impact is bounded because writing localStorage already requires same-origin script execution, so this is persistence/hardening rather than initial compromise. The unvalidated cast predates this diff; the diff touches exactly this line and adds a correctly-validated parallel module, so it is the natural place to fix it.

samples.summary: Settings persists the Select value with an unchecked cast instead of the module's own type guard
samples.evidence: `onValueChange={(value) => setDateFormat(value as DateDisplayFormat)}` persists a `string` straight into localStorage. The value originates from the two `SelectItem`s so it is not attacker-controlled today, and `getDateFormat()` re-validates on read via `isFormat` (src/lib/date-format-preference.ts:51), so there is no exploitable path — but the module already owns a guard and exporting/using it here would keep the write side from depending on a cast. Hardening only.
